_comment: The single source of truth for the Giving Day page. Edit ONLY this file, then run `python3 scripts/giving_day.py` to stamp the values into giving-day.html. Never hand-edit the regions marked GD: in the HTML — they get overwritten. See README section 12.
_status: draft = built but not linked anywhere and kept off Google. live = linked in the nav, in the sitemap, indexable. closed = page stays up, donate buttons become a thank-you. Use the publish/close commands rather than editing this by hand.
name: Giving CMU Day
_name: CMU's own name for the day. The university has run it every year since 2015, always on GivingTuesday.
_dates: CONFIRMED. CMU's own FY27 student organization training deck (Oct 2026) gives the date as Tuesday, December 1, 2026 — the 12th consecutive year. Official site: givingcmuday.cmu.edu. Keep the -05:00 offset (Pittsburgh in December) so the countdown is correct for visitors in any timezone.
_donateUrl: TBD — the 2026 campaign page does not exist until CMU builds it. CMU runs the day on GiveCampus, and each club gets a page under this pattern: https://www.givecampus.com/schools/CarnegieMellonUniversity/giving-cmu-day-2026/pages/student-organizations/<club-slug> . The club was on the 2025 edition (10 donors, $1,090). When the 2026 page exists, paste its full URL here and re-stamp. While this is empty, every donate button renders as a disabled 'coming soon' chip, so the page can never ship a dead link.
_amountParam: Query parameter the donation platform uses to preset a gift amount, so the tier buttons can jump straight to it. Set to "" if the platform doesn't support one, and the tier buttons will just link to the base page.
_askAmount: The amount every donate button on the page asks for. CMU's own training advice is to ask for "a small, non-intimidating amount like $5 or $10", and $10 is the top of that range. This is the ask; challenge.minGift below is the floor that actually counts.

challenge._minGift: $5 — confirmed in CMU's FY27 training deck, which states a $5 minimum both for the site itself and for being counted toward any match or challenge.
challenge._prizes: EMPTY ON PURPOSE. CMU does not announce the 2026 matches and challenges to student orgs until mid-November, so the page must not promise last year's numbers (2025 paid 1st $6,000, 2nd $4,000, 3rd $2,000). Fill this in when the real amounts are announced and re-stamp, or leave it empty and the aside simply does not name any figures.
challenge._note: CMU runs matches and challenges alongside the day, scored on the number of individual donors giving at least minGift. The page mentions this in one small aside and does NOT build its pitch around winning — hundreds of orgs are in that race. Its only job is to explain why a small gift counts as much as a large one. Set on=false and the aside disappears and the page stops mentioning donor counts at all.
challenge._counting: Gifts are counted by credit card holder and email address. Multiple gifts on the same card count as ONE donor, and CMU audits the email addresses. Do not give on somebody else's behalf — the page says so out loud.

video.title: Giving Day film
video._file: A video file in the repo, played straight from the site with no YouTube involved. This is the draft cut (1920x1080, 34 seconds, 14 MB). Fine on this page, but 14 MB is a slow load on phone data and a file cannot be shared anywhere but here — so when the final cut is on YouTube, fill in youtubeId below and it takes over automatically. Set this to "" to go back to the 'film coming soon' panel.
video._cmuSpec: The cut SUBMITTED TO CMU for their own fund page is a different thing from this one, and it has rules: .mp4/.mov/.avi/.mpeg/.mpg, no longer than 30 seconds, 15-20 preferred. The draft here runs 34 seconds, so it needs a trim before it goes to them. They also want one still image at 760x430, 600x400 and 600x315.
video._youtubeId: The 11-character ID from the YouTube URL (the v= part), not the whole URL. Takes precedence over 'file' when both are filled. The film's donate button carries ?utm_content=video so the platform's referral stats show what the video actually drove.
video._length: Printed on the play button, e.g. '2 min'. Leave empty to print no running time.

_goalDollars: The headline number on the progress bar. The club raised $1,090 in 2025, so $2,000 is a real but reachable stretch. 'raised' is updated by hand during the day.
_goalDonors: Secondary — printed as a line under the dollars, not as the headline. 2025: 10 donors. 40 is four times that and still honest; the challenge winners are well into the hundreds and we are not chasing them. Set to 0 to hide the people count entirely.

tiers.label: Tape, grips and chalk for a month of practices
Props and costume pieces for one showcase routine
Transport for the club and its weapons to one off-campus performance
A new broadsword or staff for the loaner rack

_tiers: Keep these concrete. 'A broadsword for the loaner rack' raises more than 'equipment'. The $10 tier leads because it is what most people give; 'flag' puts a seal on that card. Nothing here should mention competitions — the club performs, it does not compete.
whereItGoes: Weapons and mats the club lends out, so nobody has to buy gear before their first practice.
Getting people and weapons across Pittsburgh to the festivals and showcases we perform at.
Costumes and props for Lunar New Year and the spring showcase.
Keeping the barrier at zero. No dues, no equipment list, no tryout — which only works if the gear is already on the floor when someone walks in.
